episodes.title: Can both scores improve?
episodes.subtitle: A fixed candidate pool can produce a much better first page.

scenes.title: Same candidates. Better precision and better recall?
narration: Twenty candidate papers contain all ten papers judged relevant. On the first page, only two of ten are relevant. Reranking adds no paper. Can precision and recall both improve? Pause and decide which set, and which denominator, each number describes.

In the chapter’s controlled example, six relevant papers reach the first ten after reranking. Precision at ten and recall at ten both rise from point two to point six. Recall over the entire candidate pool stays at one. The boundary makes the difference.

scenes.title: Relevant to whom, for what purpose?
narration: Before counting, decide what relevant means. The same paper may help a researcher trace a method, fail to inform an undergraduate seeking an overview, and fail a reviewer’s inclusion criteria. Those verdicts concern different needs and tasks, without the paper itself changing.

The chapter separates algorithmic estimates, topical aboutness, usefulness given the reader’s knowledge, and usefulness for a task in context. This is a teaching simplification, not a complete taxonomy. A high model score is evidence the system uses, not the human judgement itself.

scenes.title: Every metric inherits the assessors’ criteria
narration: A reference interview establishes what would count as a useful answer. Evaluation writes those criteria and judgements down so systems can be compared against the same ones. Some test collections use mainly topical criteria; others encode detailed task or inclusion rules.

The formula cannot tell which conception was used. A topically relevant paper can have the wrong population, date or method, or be superseded. Report who judged, for which purpose, and whether relevance was binary or graded. The number measures agreement with those operational judgements.

scenes.title: Precision and recall divide by different things
narration: Precision divides retrieved relevant papers by retrieved papers. Recall divides retrieved relevant papers by all relevant papers under the evaluation protocol. In this example the first page holds ten records, and the complete relevance set also has ten. The denominators happen to agree numerically.

They still count different things. Before reranking, both fractions are two over ten. Afterward, both are six over ten. The complete relevant set is stipulated here. Finding ten known seeds in a live database would not establish that those are every relevant paper.

scenes.title: Reordering changes the display, not candidate membership
narration: All twenty records remain candidates before and after. Reranking moves relevant ones across the display cutoff without increasing the pool’s recall. For any later stage that only processes this fixed output, excluded records remain unavailable.

This is compatible with a better first page. Extending a fixed ranking cannot lower recall, but precision can rise or fall as the added record changes the fraction. A better ranking or representation can improve both measures at a chosen depth. The trade is not an unavoidable law between systems.

scenes.title: A fresh route can cross the candidate boundary
narration: Hybrid routes and another retrieval round can expand the cumulative pool. Their recall gain comes from newly contributed relevant records, before that new candidate boundary. Merely rearranging one existing list cannot add evidence that it never contained.

Duplicates and irrelevant additions do not raise recall. They can enlarge the pool or push useful records below a displayed cutoff. Ask where candidate generation ends, and distinguish its ceiling from recall at the depth the reader actually sees. A generated answer cannot recover an excluded source by summarising harder.

scenes.title: Where did the recall denominator come from?
narration: Precision requires judging what came back. Absolute recall also requires knowing how many relevant records the collection holds. In a live database, that total is usually unknown. A large result count does not answer the question.

Practitioners compare the relevant union found by several strategies, or test recovery of known relevant seeds. These are useful relative comparisons and regression checks, not the true denominator of an entire collection. Report the scope rather than turning known seed recovery into an absolute recall claim.

scenes.title: Choose the sensitivity and workload the task requires
narration: Ready reference often values precision; evidence reviews lean heavily on recall. The chapter’s August twenty twenty six methodological note keeps structured database searching as the formal review core, supplemented by other routes. That describes practice, not an inherent Boolean recall advantage.

Boolean strategies can miss synonyms or depend on incomplete coverage. Ranked boundaries can constrain BM twenty five as well as dense retrieval. Test the complete workflow for the task, with inspectable conditions and stated judgements. Next, we examine the different definitions of better hidden inside ranking metrics.

episodes.title: The number that ignores the rest
episodes.subtitle: Choosing a ranking metric means choosing what to reward.

scenes.title: Two relevant hits or six: can the score stay the same?
narration: Our source example improves from two to six relevant papers in the first ten. Yet its first relevant paper stays at rank one. Could a conventional ranking measure report no improvement at all? Pause and ask what that measure would have to ignore.

Reciprocal rank is one divided by the first relevant rank. Here it stays one before and after. It ignores every relevant paper following that first hit. Across queries, mean reciprocal rank averages those reciprocals. A useful number can be perfectly blind to the improvement your task values.

scenes.title: Evaluation depth is not automatically a retrieval budget
narration: Precision at k counts relevant records inside an evaluation depth. A relevant record at rank one and the same record at rank ten contribute equally to precision at ten. Rank eleven contributes nothing to that first page score.

Here k names the depth being evaluated. It need not equal the first stage candidate limit or the reranker’s budget. State all those boundaries separately. Comparing one system’s first ten with another system’s first twenty changes the question along with the system.

scenes.title: MRR rewards the first answer arriving early
narration: Mean reciprocal rank is a natural fit when the task essentially has one right answer: finding a known paper, resolving a citation, or making a factual lookup. Moving the first relevant hit upward increases its reciprocal rank.

It does not establish broad evidence coverage. Two systems can share the same first hit while one finds many additional relevant records and the other finds none. Our displayed value is a single query’s reciprocal rank; calling it a multi query comparison would imply evidence this illustration does not contain.

scenes.title: MAP rewards many relevant records placed high
narration: Average precision collects precision at the ranks where relevant papers appear, then averages using the judged relevant total for that query. For this complete twenty record illustration, the arithmetic rewards the improved placement of many relevant papers, even though the first hit stays unchanged.

Mean average precision then averages query level average precision values. It is closer to the goal of assembling a useful set, but treats relevance as binary. A marginal paper and a decisive paper count alike if both are labelled relevant. State the evaluation protocol and depth.

scenes.title: nDCG can reward decisive records more than marginal ones
narration: Normalised discounted cumulative gain accepts relevance grades and discounts contributions at lower ranks, relative to an ideal ordering at the evaluation depth. A highly relevant paper near the top can count more than a partly relevant one farther down.

That requires graded judgements and an explicit scoring convention. We are explaining the metric’s goal, not inventing grades for the source’s binary example. Its limitation remains: several highly graded records can repeat one aspect while another aspect is missing. High ranking quality does not automatically establish diverse coverage.

scenes.title: Each measure defines a different kind of better
narration: Precision at k values relevant items inside the cutoff. Mean reciprocal rank values an early first hit. Mean average precision values many binary relevant hits placed high. Normalised discounted gain values graded relevance discounted by position.

All four need judgements. These conventional relevance only measures treat record judgements independently; they do not directly reward coverage across known aspects. A metric choice is a task choice. Ask which benefit the number rewards, and which failure it cannot reveal.

scenes.title: A fair offline comparison holds the evaluation inputs still
narration: The Cranfield arrangement fixes a document collection, queries or topics, and relevance judgements. Compare systems against those same inputs. Offline test collections answer that controlled question; user studies and task based evaluations ask complementary questions.

BEIR’s cited cross collection finding is conditional on its topics and assessors: BM twenty five held up as a robust baseline, while several more expensive neural systems did better on average. That does not settle performance on your chemistry theses, languages, or local researchers’ questions.

scenes.title: Unjudged is not the same as irrelevant
narration: Large evaluations often judge the union of top results from several systems. Under the chapter’s described scoring approach, unjudged records are treated as non relevant. A genuinely useful new result outside that pool can therefore receive no credit.

This judgement pooling is different from compressing token representations into a vector. It can bias evaluation against unfamiliar retrieval approaches. Read a leaderboard as evidence about its benchmark, then ask whether the topics, criteria and judged pool resemble your task. The next film builds an evaluation whose criteria a library controls.

episodes.title: The average went up. The search got worse.
episodes.subtitle: A local regression can disappear inside an improving mean.

scenes.title: An improving average can hide a serious loss
narration: A discovery update improves the equally weighted mean of three displayed evaluation rows from point three zero to about point three three. Would you call it better? Pause before looking at the rows. What change could that average conceal?

In the chapter’s hypothetical table, the identifier row falls from point three to point one precision at ten: a two thirds relative loss. Another row improves enough to lift the mean. These are illustrative source numbers, not a product update or experiment performed for this film.

scenes.title: Read the rows before celebrating the mean
narration: The identifier query concerns S L C six A four promoter polymorphism. The hypothetical expansion drops the gene symbol. A vocabulary mismatch row rises from point two to point five. The composition row stays at point four.

That last row averages two opposite meaning queries, each judged separately. The chapter’s reported average equally weights the three displayed rows; it is not a mean of four equally weighted individual queries. Known relevant counts are seed information, not proof of exhaustive relevance. Keep both qualifications with the table.

scenes.title: Build a small set from the work the library actually does
narration: Thirty to fifty queries are a practical starting range. Use reference enquiries, loan requests, consultations and training questions, carrying the disciplines, languages and document types your library encounters. Include searches already known to fail, rather than only demonstration friendly examples.

Rerunning an established set may fit an afternoon. Constructing needs and judging hundreds of results can take much longer. Write down the task and what counts as useful, then record known relevant items and grades where staff can defend them. This is a local baseline, not an exhaustive research collection.

scenes.title: Pool both runs at the same fixed depth, then judge
narration: Choose a fixed depth, such as ten or twenty, and keep it fixed across runs. Pool and deduplicate both runs’ results at that depth. Judge every pooled record under the same written criteria, ideally without seeing which system supplied it.

Calculate precision at that depth from those judgements. Report known seed recovery separately. If a run returns fewer records, record the count and denominator convention. Otherwise a change in depth, missing judgements or an unstated denominator can masquerade as a system improvement.

scenes.title: Plant probes for the evidence each method can lose
narration: Include an exact identifier, gene name or chemical string. Include a phrase appearing only in full text you hold. Include a query whose known relevant record shares almost none of its wording. Include near identical queries with opposite meaning.

These probe a surviving lexical route, indexed units, vocabulary bridging and composition. They are diagnostic comparisons, not a guarantee that one score can explain every failure. Preserve the record and capture details needed to investigate a change. The earlier chapter supplies hypotheses about why a query lost.

scenes.title: Inspect per-query changes and ordinary variation
narration: Inspect queries that moved sharply, including differences by discipline, language or document type. A mean can absorb systematic harm to a small group of searches. A difference smaller than ordinary run to run variation may need further evidence before you can distinguish it from that variation.

Ask a vendor which queries, which collection, whose binary or graded judgements, which depth, which metric and which baseline produced the claimed gain. Then rerun the hard local questions. The local set generalises narrowly by design; its value is that the library chose the relevance criteria.

scenes.title: A faithful answer can still summarise the wrong evidence
narration: If the product also writes an answer, evaluate whether it is faithful to the retrieved material and whether each claim traces to a source that contains it. Those are additional questions, not substitutes for evaluating retrieval.

A perfectly faithful summary of the wrong ten documents is still built on the wrong shortlist. A groundedness check cannot reveal every relevant paper that retrieval missed. Keep retrieval quality, answer faithfulness and source support visible as separate requirements.

scenes.title: Make the baseline useful by rerunning it
narration: Rerun the fixed local set after a model update, index change, platform migration or before renewal. Compare per query against the saved baseline, keep the criteria and depth stable, and investigate regressions instead of letting a small mean gain settle the decision.

Measurement can identify which system performed better on these queries against these judgements. It does not explain the internal cause or make the search repeatable next year. Chapter fifteen turns to what must be recorded, inspected and required. The evaluation is useful because its comparison is explicit.
